releaseContext: 0.7.2 published Star Hider, Nick Hider replacements and local capes on the 0.7.1 renderer. Renderer research is retained for 0.7.3 and is not a completed or published backend.
decision: Build a persistent GPU scene with compact actor state, GPU visibility and indirect submission. Separate scene preparation from its OpenGL/Metal backend.
reason: Existing beta code already computes player poses and model transforms on the GPU. The larger opportunity is removing repeated Java traversal, instance preparation and driver submission around that computation, while increasing supported-model coverage.
existingWork: Argentum/Celeritas terrain meshing and instancing remain the current foundation.
GpuPlayerPipeline and GpuModelTransforms already contain compact pose jobs, compute transforms and sorting.
Current fast player paths reject active Forge hooks, custom animation poses, detailed 3D skins, hurt/death states and several extra layers.
0.7.0 already batches forced vanilla font glyphs and caches text metrics/name masking. Retained name tags, HUD and particle paths already exist.
dataFlow: Game thread extracts immutable previous/current actor states and world changes.
Stable geometry, skins, materials and actor records remain GPU-resident; uploads describe changes.
Each frame supplies current camera, partial tick, animation time and changed frame-dependent state.
GPU computes supported poses and conservative visibility, then produces indirect commands.
Actors, terrain and HUD draw through explicit passes with bounded submission and state changes.
Unsupported models and hooks keep the existing renderer, independently for each actor or pass.

phases.name: Measure the new baseline
phases.work: Capture 0.7.1 CPU/GPU phase times, allocations, submission counts and fast-path coverage on multiple PCs. Separate crowded lobby, active match, small scene and terrain-heavy scenes.
phases.gate: Identify the current critical path after the 0.7.0 text fixes. Distinguish driver waits from GPU work and use the same foreground, uncapped conditions for A/B tests.

phases.name: Persistent actor state
phases.work: Create dense immutable actor snapshots, persistent mesh/material IDs and generation-based world/resource invalidation. Retain the existing backend first, so scene extraction can be verified independently.
phases.gate: No worker reads mutable Minecraft objects or calls GL. Frame interpolation and camera state remain current; entity-ID reuse, resource reload, world change and server switch cannot reuse stale state.

phases.name: Resident actor rendering
phases.work: Use compact previous/current state plus per-frame parameters to generate bone/instance data and grouped indirect commands. Reuse geometry, texture tables and command storage across frames.
phases.gate: Show actual submitted actor count, rejected actors and reasons. No per-frame GPU-to-CPU visibility readback or full vanilla model traversal on the supported path.

phases.name: Real client feature coverage
phases.work: Add explicit adapters for Arcadium animations, hurt/death, armor, held items, capes, 3D skin layers, glint, cosmetics and color-saturation passes. Preserve Forge rendering callbacks instead of globally bypassing them. Preserve the released 0.7.2 local Cape module and revision-aware Nick Hider when reusing actor/material/name-tag state. Reproduce and repair the reported held-item rendering corruption with real Forge guests; compare first-person and both F5 directions, self and other players, with optimization enabled and disabled.
phases.gate: Known supported effects render identically and callbacks run once with the expected state. Unknown hooks fall back per actor. A fast path that rejects most real players is not accepted as a completed optimization.

phases.name: GPU terrain command preparation
phases.work: Audit pinned Argentum/Celeritas coverage, then move remaining section traversal and command preparation into GPU-visible scene buffers. Reuse existing meshing and full-detail geometry.
phases.gate: Newly exposed terrain appears in the same frame after camera motion or block changes. Start with conservative frustum tests; occlusion cannot hide players, bridge edges or newly revealed blocks.

phases.name: Metal backend prototype
phases.work: Reuse the same scene/pass description on Metal. Keep Pylon/SDL window ownership and implement the Skiko/Compose, Cera, text, blur, framebuffer and input connections before calling it an Arcadium renderer.
phases.gate: Compare native Metal against current Argentum on Apple Silicon and Intel macOS 12.7.6 hardware. Preserve the supported OpenGL path when device features or integration are insufficient.

phases.name: Cross-device adoption
phases.work: Measure paired runs on the tester laptop, development PC, weaker Windows GPU, Apple Silicon and supported Intel Mac. Add one selectable backend and focused controls within the existing three Beta categories.
phases.gate: Publish complete option values and actual fast-path use, together with visual, frame-time, memory and latency evidence. Keep detailed status on the diagnostics page.

platforms.primary: OpenGL compute plus indirect submission, chosen by actual capabilities.
platforms.fallback: Existing Argentum path or CPU preparation with batching.
platforms.constraint: Do not assume indirect-count or bindless support from a vendor name. An optional NVIDIA mesh path is a later optimization, not the portable foundation.

platforms.primary: Prototype Metal against the same scene description.
platforms.constraint: Legacy GL calls and Skiko/UI surfaces need a real backend connection. Changing the API name alone is not sufficient.

platforms.primary: Probe Metal device limits and compare on the actual supported hardware.
platforms.constraint: Keep existing OS support. Do not require modern Metal features or Windows OpenGL compute support on this path.

adoptionGoals.performanceGoal: Aim for at least 2x average FPS in a demonstrably CPU-bound crowded scene; this is a development target, not a measured result or a forecast.
adoptionGoals.frameTimeGoal: Aim for at least 30% higher 1% low in the target scene. Reject repeatable regressions above 3% in ordinary scenes or low-end fallback paths.
adoptionGoals.latency: Use current camera/input and do not grow the render-ahead queue to inflate FPS. Compare input-to-present behavior with the existing renderer.
adoptionGoals.visuals: No reduced resolution, lower render distance, removed effects or frame generation in the default comparison. Check text, HUD, name tags, F5 held items, transparency and animation poses against the reference.
adoptionGoals.resources: Bound resident memory, upload queues and caches. Test long sessions, resource reload, resizing, world/server changes and device/backend failure.
adoptionGoals.evidence: Actual gains remain unmeasured. Use repeatable local fixtures plus live Hypixel validation; never transfer another project's reported multiplier to Arcadium.

invariants: No changes to game tick frequency, packets, movement, combat logic or server-visible position.
No forced opt-in or invisible disabling of Forge callbacks or existing client modules.
Keep OpenGL fallback available before expanding to Vulkan/Metal. Backend switching can require a restart.
Do not add more than two or three Beta categories; put verified Hypixel benefits first.

references.use: Separate command/pass/backend ownership, compact GPU poses and fallback design.
references.condition: MPL-2.0. Reference at the design stage; any future incorporation must keep the applicable notices and source conditions.

references.use: Legacy 1.8.9 Metal hooks and full-pipeline integration boundaries.
references.condition: LGPL-3.0. Its Forge/LWJGL2 window and input replacement is not a drop-in match for Arcadium Ornithe/Pylon/Skiko. No code is included by this release.

references.use: Study the GPU command-generation architecture as a reference only.
references.condition: The inspected license says All rights reserved and Do not redistribute. Do not copy or redistribute its implementation in Arcadium.

references.use: Optional vendor-specific mesh/submission approach after a portable path exists.
references.condition: The upstream README requires Turing or newer NVIDIA hardware. It cannot be the only Windows or Mac path.

references.use: Preserve existing instancing, meshing, text and occlusion work and avoid rebuilding equivalent optimizations.
references.condition: Keep the user's existing Argentum arrangement. Audit exact Celeritas/backend interfaces before changing integration.

references.use: A possible window integration point for a Metal backend; it still needs engineering and native validation.

releaseFixes.status: Native mouse regression passed on the same Main20 artifact as the input-layout repair: eight cases, four original local-server command echoes, three book page changes and one raw suggestion. Full renderer/release qualification remains open.
releaseFixes.requirement: Restore native clickable chat commands and interactive book text, including Nick Hider enabled, without changing original server ClickEvent payloads or native URL confirmation.
gates: Native literal hit-testing retains displayed text, inherited style, click/hover/insertion, siblings and copy behavior.
Local owned runtime verifies chat RUN_COMMAND/SUGGEST_COMMAND and book CHANGE_PAGE/RUN_COMMAND using real mouse routing.
Nick Hider aliases and revision/no-double-replacement behavior remain correct; commands and metadata sent to the server are unchanged.
Check shared legacy/modern paths and state the actual affected version scope; no real gift redemption in tests.

releaseFixes.status: Implemented with a shared raw/display projection and bounded revision-aware reuse. Main20 passed 674 unit tests and 20 native Vanilla/Inter field cases with exact RGBA references, raw editing/copy checks and 2740 direct native-method mouse hits. Physical keyboard/send and custom resource-font checks remain separate gates.
releaseFixes.requirement: Render custom Nick Hider replacements coherently when replacement text has a different length, including editable chat fields, without changing raw text, server commands or click metadata.
gates: One non-cascading display projection controls rendering, caret, selection, scrolling and mouse positions.
Native editing, clipboard, trim/source indices and outgoing text remain raw; shorter, longer, empty and multiple rules are covered.
Formatting, Unicode/emoji boundaries, vanilla/Inter/resource fonts and Password Hider retain correct behavior.
No new unbounded cache or repeated unchanged-text projection rebuild; actual owned input-field mouse/keyboard regression proof is required.

releaseFixes.status: Implemented native SDL UI cursor visibility in the legacy Core. Both legacy Core variants build; 116 CPU policy checks pass. Windows 1.8.9 paired old/new Core runs pass all nine 5/120 FPS, menu, reload, fullscreen/windowed and gameplay-grab states, with real Root mouse events and native SDL/Win32 visibility. No cursor-motion rate, FPS-gain or native 1.7.10 claim; full renderer/release qualification remains open.
releaseFixes.requirement: Keep menu pointer motion responsive when game rendering slows, using the native hardware cursor where supported while preserving normal UI hit testing and grabbed in-game aiming.
gates: Identify each affected shared, legacy and modern cursor path and verify the actual native capability and fallback.
Check low and normal frame rates, cursor style and hotspot, UI scale, focus, grabs, fullscreen changes and cursor resource lifetime.
Do not add a separate rendering or input thread or change game, combat or networking behavior.
